subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: After the native Code Mode policy mapping is fixed, should OpenClaw accept this scoped positive-delivery path that depends on a Codex runtime emitting the required PreToolUse event and routes policy-active sessions through unified exec/fresh thread binding?
rationale: The remaining choice affects tool-execution enforcement, existing Codex session continuity, and compatibility with packaged Codex behavior; code review can identify the tradeoffs but cannot choose the security product boundary for maintainers.

options.title: Accept After Mapping And Runtime Proof
options.body: Repair the Code Mode mapping, require proof or packaging evidence for the Codex runtime prerequisite, then let maintainers review the scoped unified-exec/fresh-thread tradeoff for merge.

options.title: Pause Behind Packaged Codex
options.body: Keep the PR draft until @openai/codex in OpenClaw's package surface definitively contains the required native PreToolUse behavior.

options.title: Prefer Fail-Closed Alternative
options.body: Do not land this positive-delivery approach and instead pursue a fail-closed or native-surface-disable design from the related draft PRs.

recommendation.title: Accept After Mapping And Runtime Proof
recommendation.body: Repair the Code Mode mapping, require proof or packaging evidence for the Codex runtime prerequisite, then let maintainers review the scoped unified-exec/fresh-thread tradeoff for merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the native relay and CLI startup policy surfaces and is the best available owner for the security-boundary tradeoff.
